classification.difficultyReason: Derives an exact conversion equation from a graph and combines two exchange rates through Australian dollars.

content.prompt: The relationship between British pounds $(p)$ and Australian dollars $(d)$ on a particular day is shown in the graph.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Write the direct variation equation relating pounds to dollars in the form $p = md$.
Leave $m$ as a fraction.

spec.description: First-quadrant graph with unit grid subdivisions, stronger vertical grid lines every five Australian dollars, arrowed axes, a straight line through the origin and the marked point (7,4). Axis titles and variable labels remain separate.
spec.mathematics: p = (4/7)d; grid 0 ≤ d ≤ 20 and 0 ≤ p ≤ 15; labelled d ticks 0,5,10,15,20 and p ticks 2,4,6,8,10,12,14.
spec.answerVisibility: The line and labelled point are permanent student givens; the conversion equation is answer-only.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The relationship between Japanese yen $(y)$ and Australian dollars $(d)$ on the same day is given by the equation $y = 76d$. Convert 93 100 Japanese yen to British pounds.

answer.worked:
First convert Japanese yen to Australian dollars:
$$\begin{align*}93100 &= 76d \\ d &= \frac{93100}{76} \\ d &= 1225\end{align*}$$
Now convert Australian dollars to British pounds using the equation from part (a):
$$\begin{align*}p &= \frac{4}{7}\times1225 \\ p &= 700\end{align*}$$
The amount is £700.
